messages:
maya: quick question — when an SLO alert fires from the console, how do we surface notify backpressure (webhook 429s / rate limits) in the UI?

sam: do you mean in the preview pane or in the live alert timeline?

maya: both. Preview should show whether alerts would be throttled for that policy (so users don't expect 1:1 deliveries). Live timeline should show suppressed/dropped counts and link to retry/queue metrics.

jordan: implementation-wise we currently treat 429 from notifiers as transient and retry with exponential backoff in the dispatcher. but we don't expose that anywhere — only logs.

anya: +1 for a visible metric. UX idea: show a small badge next to notify policy "expected deliveries: 87% (est) — 13% suppressed". We can compute from recent webhook response codes and rate_limit headers.

sam: curious about ownership: should the notifier return metadata to the control plane? e.g. headers: `X-Notify-Queue-Len` or `X-Notify-Rate-Window` so console can show real-time status.

maya: exact idea I had. If a downstream webhook emits `429` with `Retry-After`, we surface a predicted suppression window in the rule preview. Also useful for canarying a policy during rollout.

jordan: small API sketch: `POST /v1/notify/dispatch` -> 202 + `{queued: true, eta_ms: 450}` or 429 + `{queued: false, reason: "rate_limit"}`. Frontend can show a simulated delivery chart.

anya: caveat — we must not leak PII or auth details from third-party webhooks. Only surface aggregated counters & anonymized states.

sam: question for eng-sre — if we start showing predicted suppression, do we need a new telemetry pipeline? right now we only ship per-request status to logs.

eng-notify-bot: deploy: notifier-service v2.14 deployed to prod (hash: 9a7f3). New metrics endpoints enabled behind flag `notifier.expose_delivery_stats=true`.

maya: perfect — can we gate the UI behind the same feature flag? I don't want the console to show partial data.

jordan: yep. backend flag + feature flag in console. Also need a compact signal we can compute cheaply: sliding-window success_rate + recent 429_count. low-cost query: `sum(success_count)/sum(total)` over 5m partitioned by policy_id.

anya: UX nit: the preview should let users simulate tenant-level quotas too — e.g., "if tenant X has 100 alerts/min quota, how many would be delivered?" That avoids surprises when customers turn on a policy.

maya: agree. That means preview needs a deterministic evaluator that knows per-tenant quota rules and current queue lengths. Could be a local simulation in the frontend calling a `/v1/alerts/preview` API with `simulate_quota=true`.

sam: internal API debate: do we make preview purely client-side (fast, approximate) or server-side (accurate, heavier)? I vote server-side for correctness, but return a lightweight summary to avoid blocking the UI.

jordan: server-side but cache results for 10s. Also allow an optional `detail=true` for deeper traces.

maya: next steps: 1) eng-notify to add header + small JSON body for queued/estimated_ETA; 2) telemetry team to emit `notify_delivery_rate` per policy; 3) console PR for preview badge + detailed modal behind FF.

anya: I'll draft a tiny design mock with the badge + modal showing: "expected delivered / suppressed / queued" and a toggle for "simulate tenant quota".

sam: I'll pick up the backend API change. I'll add the `simulate_quota` param to `POST /v1/alerts/preview` and wire the existing rate metrics in.

maya: awesome. can we add a small runbook entry: if `expected delivered < 50%` show recommended actions (lower frequency, change transport to email/oncall).

jordan: noted. I'll add a short doc in the notifier repo.

maya: thanks everyone. tagging @anya and @sam for followups. :thumbsup:

eng-notify-bot: note: metric `notifier.delivery.success_rate{policy_id}` emitted to metrics cluster `metrics-prod`.
